subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Ghost Festivals of Asia
description: A quick, practical guide to Ghost Festivals of Asia.

hook.text: In the Chinese Hungry Ghost Festival, the gates of the underworld open and spirits roam for a month.

buildup.text: Families burn paper money, paper houses, and paper phones. The dead need supplies in the afterlife.

discovery.text: Japan's Obon festival welcomes ancestor spirits with lanterns. At the end, lanterns float down rivers.

twist.text: These festivals assume the dead still have needs and feelings. They're not gone—they're just in another place.

climax.text: Asian ghost festivals make death a temporary separation, not a wall. The barrier thins on certain days.

punchline.text: The gates open once a year. Be ready.

quiz.question: What do families burn during the Hungry Ghost Festival?
options: Paper money and paper goods for the dead
